The `// fire-and-forget to forward backend` comment does not match the behavior here: the code blocks on `.get(10, MILLISECONDS)` and rethrows as a `RuntimeException` on failure. Two concerns:

1. A 10 ms timeout is very aggressive for a gRPC round-trip to another container — the first export in particular has to establish the channel, which will typically take longer than 10 ms and hit `TimeoutException`. Because the throw happens before `metricRequests.add(request)` (line 452), a forwarding failure drops the metric batch entirely and returns an error to the agent, which can make `verifyMetrics(...)` flaky.
2. Forwarding to weaver is auxiliary validation; a forwarding error should not break the primary metric capture. Consider logging the failure instead of throwing (and restoring the interrupt flag on `InterruptedException` rather than wrapping it).

Note that reworking this to a local variable would also let you drop the now-redundant `requireNonNull(forwardStub, ...)` on line 441 (and its `java.util.Objects.requireNonNull` import), since a local reference narrows nullness for NullAway without the extra guard.

This comment is grammatically incorrect and hard to parse ("not part supported platforms"). It reads more clearly as "This is not part of supported platforms and is only captured from the test environment".

threads.body: [General] This only reads advice attached directly to a metric (and directly to resource attributes). Weaver attaches findings at the pertinent nested level—for example, missing required metric attributes on data points and attribute type mismatches on the attributes themselves—so those violations never reach `violationCount` and invalid telemetry can pass. Traverse all nested `live_check_result.all_advice` entries in each sample.

threads.body: [General] If the `/stop` request or JSON parsing fails, this method throws before `super.stop()` and leaves the container running. Put the container cleanup in a `finally` block so teardown is reliable on the failure path.

[General] `build()` creates a `ManagedChannel`, but only the stub is retained and neither replacement nor test teardown shuts the channel down. Keep the channel itself and close it when forwarding is reset and after the server stops to avoid leaking gRPC resources across parameterized runs.

[General] A 10 ms timeout also covers the first gRPC channel connection and container round trip, which can legitimately exceed that threshold and make forwarding flaky. Use a seconds-scale timeout (or a stub deadline) instead.

[General] Weaver initializes every registry metric and attribute in these statistics maps with count `0`. Collecting only `fieldNames()` therefore makes the “seen” sets contain definitions that were never reported, so `checkRegistered` can pass without observing the expected telemetry. Preserve/filter the counts and include only entries whose count is greater than zero; the JVM expectations should then cover only telemetry this test actually emits.

replies.body: @SylvainJuge this looks like a potential problem

You are correct, the registered metrics that were not reported have a count of zero in the weaver result.

I've fixed that in d326832b82.

For example, one example where this was an issue is that the `jvm.gc.duration` metric is registered as it's part of the upstream semantic conventions, however it's not being reported as the JMX implementation can't capture it (as it's an histogram).

While some attributes are marked as "optional", I don't think we have an equivalent for metrics in the semconv yaml, most of them are marked as "recommended" in docs, and knowing when they should be present or not depends on the context.

threads.body: [General] The `ManagedChannel` created here is discarded, so it cannot be shut down. Each parameterized invocation replaces the stub while leaving the previous channel alive, retaining gRPC executors and transports through the test run. Store the channel separately and shut it down both when replacing the forwarding endpoint and when the OTLP server is stopped.

[General] The forwarding channel is only shut down by the next invocation's `beforeEach()`. After the final invocation it remains open when the OTLP server is stopped, and a validation failure also skips cleanup. Reset the forwarding backend in this teardown using `finally`.
